name: Ui_MonsterBook_EntryDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of one monster-book entry row: installs the entry vtable, releases the embedded node block's two links and its two pack handles, runs the shared UI base destructor and frees the row.
evidence: NEW: the named caller Ui_SenrekiWindow_DtorBody (0x00296E8C, R3_021) destroys this object in the same teardown as Ui_AdventureLogWindow_Dtor and Ui_QuestWindow_Dtor - the three tabs of the records/history (Senreki) window - so the monster-book entry reading is supported on top of the textbook deleting-dtor shape (Ui_ReleaseTwoHandles -> Pack_ReleaseHandle x2 -> Ui_Object_DtorBase -> free).

name: Ui_MonsterBook_EntryDtorB
summary: Non-deleting twin of 0x00419EC8: identical vtable install, node-block unlink, two pack-handle releases and UI base destructor, but it leaves the storage to the caller (no free) - the compiler's base-object destructor variant.
evidence: Same body as the now-supported 0x00419EC8 (whose class is fixed by the named caller Ui_SenrekiWindow_DtorBody) minus the trailing free call.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_IconTableDtor
summary: Deleting destructor trampoline of an embedded window sub-object: stores the incoming vtable, releases the handle pair at +0x124, runs Ui_Object_DtorBase on the enclosing object (self-0x124) and frees it. Only the callers (item-info-window teardown) tie it to a class.
evidence: Its only callers are maybe_Ui_ItemInfoWindow_DeletingDtor and maybe_Ui_ItemInfoWindow_Dtor_2, so it is an embedded sub-object destructor of that window family; the 'IconTable' label still comes only from the 0x002BB660 constructor and is not verified.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_IconTableDtorBase
summary: Non-deleting tail-jump variant of 0x002BB758: stores the vtable, releases the handle pair at +0x124 and branches to Ui_Object_DtorBase on the enclosing object without freeing.
evidence: Confirmed as the non-deleting partner by the identical first half and the tail branch to the named Ui_Object_DtorBase; no named caller fixes which sub-object class it belongs to, so the maybe_ prefix stays.

name: maybe_Party_GetCharaFlagBit1
summary: Reads the character id at member+0xC8, looks up a small data-manager row for it and returns bit 1 of that row's flags byte (+4). The meaning of the bit is unknown, but it is a per-character data flag, not a PartyMember field.
evidence: CORRECTED: the named caller Ui_EquipWindow_LoadPreviewModel (0.55) calls this right after func_0035EB98(member) and combines the result with maybe_Party_IsReserveMember, so it is a character-table flag - but the row comes from a bounded data-manager accessor, NOT the 0x434-stride CharacterRecord documented in FACTS, so 'MemberRecord' in the old name was wrong. The bit's semantics still have no string or user evidence.

name: maybe_Actor_Action_CreateOpcode30
summary: Factory for a named game-object descriptor used as a field-action tree node: gets the descriptor from Gfx_ObjectDesc_Init, installs the field-action vtable, writes opcode 0x1E at +0x2C and the data word at +0x28 and clears the two state bytes.
evidence: The named caller Ui_EquipWindow_LoadPreviewModel (0.55) shows the factory is also used by the equipment preview, so it is a shared action-node factory; the opcode constant 0x1E is real, but the 'Actor_Action' subsystem label is still inherited from the first pass.

name: maybe_Gfx_ObjectDesc_CtorA
summary: Constructor of a Gfx_ObjectDesc subclass: obtains the descriptor through Gfx_ObjectDesc_Init, installs vtable 0x0076E04C and stores the caller's word in descriptor slot +0x28.
evidence: The allocator (Gfx_ObjectDesc_Init) and the vtable discriminator 0x0076E04C are explicit, so the constructor role is certain; no named caller or sibling identifies the concrete descriptor class, so 'CtorA' remains a placeholder.

name: maybe_Gfx_RenderObject_ReleaseBindings
summary: Conditionally releases the three resource bindings held by a render object: the texture binding at +0x68 (when +0x90 is clear), the material binding at +0x94 (when +0x28 is set and +0x30 clear) and the material set at +0x98.
evidence: The three release callees are named in the readable doc, but the decompiled body is damaged (all accesses go through unaff_r4, the argument register was lost), so the exact owner/field mapping cannot be verified - keep maybe_ at <=0.3 per the damaged-body rule.

name: Ui_TextListWidget_BaseDtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor of the base class of the text-list widget: restores base table 0x007601A8, destroys the three embedded binding sub-objects at -0x38/-0x6C/-0x98, runs the scene-object root destructor and frees the block.
evidence: CORRECTED: the named caller Ui_TextListWidget_DtorDelete (0x00478C34, 0.60) does 'bl 0x2C6A60' for its base destructor (asm at 0x00478C38); 0x2C6A0C is the same base-class destructor body ending in 'b 0x10F6CC' (free), i.e. the deleting variant, while 0x2C6A60 is its non-deleting twin. The old 'Ui_Screen_SubObjectsDtor' label was a guess.

name: Ui_TextListWidget_BaseDtor
summary: Non-deleting base-class destructor of the text-list widget: installs base table 0x007601A8, restores and releases the three embedded Gfx binding sub-objects and tail-jumps to the scene-object root destructor. Ghidra split this function: the real entry is 0x002C6A60 (which loads the table), 0x002C6A64 is four bytes into it.
evidence: CORRECTED: the same class as 0x002C6A0C (vtable 0x007601A8) and the target of Ui_TextListWidget_DtorDelete's base-destructor call at 0x00478C38 ('bl 0x2C6A60'). The 4-byte offset is the documented mid-function-split Ghidra trap, so the old 'Gfx_SceneObject_Dtor' label was wrong.

name: Ui_JackpotScreen_UpdateWidgets
summary: Per-frame update of the jackpot screen: advances the camera track, applies the fade colours, updates the two reel models with the current value and ticks the optional child widget.
evidence: The now-named callees Ui_JackpotCamera_UpdateTrack and Ui_JackpotScreen_SetFadeColors fix the screen, and the body feeds the same value into the two reel models; only the unrecovered jump table at the callback tail keeps the confidence moderate.

name: Ui_Screen_CommitPendingControl
summary: Commits the screen's pending control: if the owner and its pending control exist it binds that control slot at owner+0x1E18, marks the owner's layout dirty (f_94 = 1) and invokes the owner's layout virtual at f_11C+0x78.
evidence: CORRECTED: the body is byte-for-byte the same operation as the guide-window helper 0x0036A494, which the confident callers Ui_GuideWindow_LayoutPage / Ui_GuideWindow_NextPage invoke when a page becomes current; 'InvokeNextCallback' described only the last instruction and hid the binding/dirty steps.

name: maybe_Ui_SetWidgetEnabled
summary: Widget state vtable slot: when the widget is still uninitialised (+0x14 clear) and the new state is non-zero it raises the UI core's mode word at +0x94, then forwards the flag to the object's state setter.
evidence: Both callers (Ui_DiveWindow_InitPanes, Ui_DiveWindow_ResetSelection) pass a boolean-like flag through this slot, but the tail-called setter 0x0029126C is inside a Ghidra-split function and unnamed, so 'enabled' vs 'visible' is still unverified.

name: maybe_Map_FindCellInDirectionAlt
signature: void maybe_Map_FindCellInDirectionAlt(u32* out, int cell, u32 x, u32 y, int* origin, int dir)
summary: Third directional cell search: picks the dominant axis of the cell rectangle around the origin, then walks the Field2D cell layers with the same attribute queries as the other finders and writes the hit cell or -1.
evidence: Called from the named Gfx_Trail_AdvancePathNode together with the other direction finders, so the family is right; the 0xF/0x10 attribute lookups and the short at cell+0x1C still decide the layer and are not explained, so it stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Map_TestCellBlockedFlags
signature: u32 maybe_Map_TestCellBlockedFlags(u32 x, u32 y, u32* pos, u32 arg4)
summary: Resolves the Field2D cell at (x,y) and its attribute record for pos, then returns 1 when either attribute 0x20 or 0x40 is present (the pair the trail direction finders treat as impassable).
evidence: Called from the named Gfx_Trail_AdvancePathNode next to the direction finders and uses the same attribute helper with the same two constants; that the flags mean 'blocked' is still an inference from usage, not proven.

name: Battle_ActorModel_SetLocatorPairFromActor
signature: void Battle_ActorModel_SetLocatorPairFromActor(void* self, void* actor, u32 arg3)
summary: Clears the two visibility flags on a battle actor model attachment and caches the locator ids of the actor's action row (u16 f_138/f_12E) into the attachment's f_4C/f_4E.
evidence: CORRECTED: all named callers are battle pose/motion code (Battle_ActorAction_UpdateComposite, Battle_ActorAction_UpdateWeaponLocators) and the row comes from the action-row accessor 0x0063FD24 (FACTS: Game_GetDataManager action rows). 'Gfx_ModelAttach' hid the battle subsystem; the locator-pair part of the old name was right.

name: maybe_Model_Actor_HideAttachment
summary: Hides an actor attachment: sends state 4 through vtable slot +0x3C and clears the shown flag at +0x26F. Mirror image of 0x00377AC4.
evidence: Its callers (Battle_ActorAction_UpdateMotion, Battle_ActionModel_UpdateAttachmentVisibility) support the attachment-visibility role, but the mirror function 0x00377AC4 is itself still maybe_, and the owning class remains unidentified.

name: maybe_Gfx_SceneNode_SetIndexPair
summary: Applies a two-word index pair to the Gfx scene stored at self+0x14: it removes the node at indices[1] through Gfx_Scene_RemoveNode and passes indices[0] to a second scene helper (Ghidra split the callee).
evidence: CORRECTED: the first callee is the named (and destructive) Gfx_Scene_RemoveNode, so the old 'SetUV' reading is unsupported; the two ints are plainly two scene indices. What the second, split helper does is still unknown, so maybe_ stays.

name: Field_Prop_HandleCommand
signature: void Field_Prop_HandleCommand(FieldProp* self, u32 message, const char* name, u32 arg4)
summary: Scene-node command handler for a field prop: on command 7 with a matching name it switches the prop to interactive state 4, activates its children and, if the player's box overlaps, starts the interaction; every command is then forwarded to the children.
evidence: The tail call is the named Field_SceneNode_ForwardCommand / Field_SceneNode_ForwardCommandToChildren, which makes the command-handler role explicit and replaces the old 'OnTouchNotify' implication.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_Ctor_vt762760
summary: Small UI-object constructor: runs Ui_Object_CtorBase, installs vtable 0x00762760 and clears the single object pointer at +0x4C.
evidence: CORRECTED: its only named caller is Ui_SkillPanel_Ctor (0x0036F878), not an item box; the body is the generic Ui_Object_CtorBase + vtable + one cleared pointer, so 'Menu_ItemBox' was unsupported. The vtable address is used as the honest discriminator.

name: Data_SetIndexedLabel
signature: void Data_SetIndexedLabel(int unusedCtx, int index, const u16* label)
summary: Stores a 7-character UTF-16 label in the indexed 0x8C-stride label table in GameWork: clears the four leading words of the row and copies the fixed-length string with zero padding.
evidence: The body is fully unambiguous (base + index*0x8C, four cleared words, std_wcsncpy of 7 wide chars) and both named callees (Game_GetWork, std_wcsncpy) confirm it; only what the table is used for remains unknown, which the generic 'Data_' prefix admits.

name: Text_ScanControlTags
signature: int Text_ScanControlTags(u32 ignored, const u16* text)
summary: Scans a compiled message stream for the page/line control tag (opcode 4, operand 2..0x0F), copies the text runs around the tag into stack wide-string buffers and returns the last operand seen (or 0 when there is no such tag).
evidence: Disassembly 0x003077BC..0x003079D4 calls the documented UTF-16 strlen (0x00100B74) and std_wcsncpy (0x00100A74), builds two stack buffers and returns the tag operand; the readable C only shows the truncated tail (the 'does not return' marking is a Ghidra misread). Whether the value is a page id or a line count is still unknown, which the neutral name does not claim.

name: Shop_SellItem
signature: u32 Shop_SellItem(u32* screen, int itemId, int count, int inventorySlot, int memberIndex)
summary: Sell path: looks the item up, removes the units from a party member's inventory (memberIndex < 0x1F) or from the bag, and credits the party gold with record field +0x1C x count. Returns 1 on success, 0 when the item is unknown or the count is invalid.
evidence: CORRECTED: its twin Shop_BuyItemForMember (0x0031120C) passes -price*count to the same ItemBag gold helper 0x00613FC0, while this function passes +record[+0x1C]*count (the sell-price field, not the buy price +0x18) and calls Member_RemoveItemAtSlot / the bag removal helper 0x006115BC - so the old 'BuyItemToBag' had the transaction direction backwards. Named callers include Ui_ShopItemList_BeginBuy / Ui_ItemScreen_ConfirmEntryEx.

name: Field2D_TestAreaPassable
signature: u32 Field2D_TestAreaPassable(void* self, const int* point)
summary: Tests a 2x2 sample of map cells starting at point+self offsets with Map_IsCellPassable; if all four are passable it asks Field_QueryOccludersInBoxLayer whether the box is clear and returns 1 for a clear area, 0 otherwise.
evidence: CORRECTED: the callers are the named Actor2D movement/turn functions (Actor2DMoveEx, Actor2DTurnTarget, Actor2DRunNotSyncDir, Actor2DSlowWalkNotSyncDir) plus Ui_Overlay_TryTouchSelect, and the callees are Map_IsCellPassable / Field_QueryOccludersInBoxLayer - this is 2D field/map collision, not UI hit testing, so the old Ui_ prefix was wrong.

name: maybe_Field_Placement_TestAreaC
signature: void maybe_Field_Placement_TestAreaC(FieldPlacementResult* out, int* base, int* offset, int* size, u32 testDesc, int manager)
summary: Third placement-area test: rejects the rectangle if Field_HitTestActors finds an actor, walks every cell with Map_IsCellPassable, confirms the scene rectangle, and writes the accepted origin plus the 1/0 result into out.
evidence: Callees (Field_HitTestActors, Map_IsCellPassable, maybe_Field_QuerySceneRect) confirm the 'test an area' shape, but the only caller 0x002D791C is itself unnamed and the 'C' merely records that it is the third of three near-identical variants.

name: Battle_ActionSequence_AnnounceAction
summary: Announces the currently acting unit's action: unless the unit is a special case it spawns a battle popup entry (Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForActorPair) with the action id and target; otherwise it pushes the member action message from the unit record's +0x2AA. Both branches return the battle UI block at world+0x5C+0x4238.
evidence: CORRECTED: both named callees (Battle_Ui_PushMemberActionMessage and Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForActorPair) are announcement paths, so the function is not merely a 'spawn popup' - the popup is only the first branch. The old name also mis-stated the call as returning a new popup rather than the shared battle UI block.

name: Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_PushActionMessage
signature: u64 Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_PushActionMessage(BattleUiMemberWidget* self, u32 arg2, u32* arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Member-widget vtable slot: pushes the action message id stored in the member record (+0x2AA) through Battle_Ui_PushMemberActionMessage, runs the widget's own update slot at +0x48 and returns the battle UI block at world+0x5C+0x4238.
evidence: The body is the same announcement tail as the now-corrected 0x003205BC and both callees (Battle_Ui_PushMemberActionMessage, Os_GetGameWork) are named; the widget class is still inferred from the slot layout, so the confidence stays at 0.5.

name: Ui_BattleWindow_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a battle sub-window: builds the window base with Ui_WindowBase_Ctor, installs the class vtable and clears the two state words at +0x70/+0x74.
evidence: The two named callers Ui_BattleWindowManager_CreateWindows and Ui_SetupDouguWindow both construct it as a battle sub-window, and the body is a plain Ui_WindowBase_Ctor + vtable + two cleared words; the exact window class is not distinguishable from the body alone.

name: maybe_Ui_EntryListWindow_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a small list-owning window: window base, vtable 0x00766B74, sentinel byte +0x6E = 0xFF and one intrusive list head at +0x70 initialised to empty (three self-pointers, zero count).
evidence: The single named caller is Ui_BattleWindowManager_CreateWindows, which is not enough to name the concrete pane, and the vtable has no named siblings; the body does prove one (not two) list heads, which is what the corrected first-pass summary says.

name: Ui_BattleBindWindow_CtorB
summary: Second constructor variant of the 0x8C-byte 'win_bind' battle window (vtable 0x00769940): builds the window base and clears the seven state words +0x70..+0x88. Chosen when the battle work display byte (+0x4244) selects the other UI configuration.
evidence: Its caller Ui_BattleWindow_CreateMainWindow allocates exactly 0x8C bytes and loads the 'win_bind' pane, and the twin constructor 0x003D2260 is the same pattern with the other vtable; this fixes both the class and the A/B variant.

name: maybe_Ui_SlotPanel_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a small tweenable UI panel: UI object base, vtable 0x00763F74, two embedded animation-reference lists at +0x4C and +0x9C and cleared tween fields; returns the panel base 0x9C bytes before the innermost list.
evidence: Ui_Object_CtorBase and Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor (twice) are named, which fixes the 'two animation-list tween panel' shape, and its user is the named Ui_CreditTextWindow_Ctor; the concrete pane class is still unidentified, so the inherited 'SlotPanel' label stays maybe_.

name: Ui_TextSpan_Rebuild
summary: Rebuilds a text widget's span array from the current item list: applies the current entries to the span array at self+0x7C, appends one span per item id (using the entry's extra byte), clamps the count to at least 1 and notifies the owner through vtable +0x6C.
evidence: The named callees Text_ApplyToSpanArray, Item_LookupRecord and Container_SetCountFromByteSize make the rebuild explicit. The item ids here only select inline item glyphs/names inside a text span (not an item bag or inventory operation), so the Text/Glyph name check does not apply.

name: maybe_Ui_DiveResultWindow_ShowItem
summary: Shows one item in a result text widget: clears the pending byte at text+0x12C, resolves the item reference to a display row and runs text command 6 with (row, item byte +0xB), or command 0 when the reference resolves to nothing.
evidence: The named callees Ui_ListItemRef_ResolveRow, Text_SetCommandArgs and Text_ExecuteCommand confirm the item-text-command role, but there are no callers and nothing in the body proves the 'DiveResultWindow' class label, so it stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Row_SetItemIcon
summary: Sets a row's item icon and label: resolves the item to a display model, stores the icon id at +0x138 and runs text command 5 or 6 (or 7 when the item is missing) so the row shows the icon/name; finally updates the attached text widget's width.
evidence: The body is explicit (Ui_ListItemRef_ResolveRow, Text_SetCommandArgs, Text_ExecuteCommand 5/6/7, icon id at +0x138), but no callers or vtable siblings fix the row class, so 'Ui_Row' remains a structural label.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_OnModelReady
summary: After a model/attachment becomes available: resolves the object handle, validates the handle at +0xB3, and when the ready flag +0x2C8 is set calls the actor's two visibility slots with mode 4 and applies the visibility state.
evidence: The callees (Ui_ResolveObjectHandle, Field_HandleIsValid, Field_Actor_ApplyVisibilityState) are now named, but no caller shows what triggers it and the 'OnModelReady' event semantics cannot be read from the body.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_OnBreakCommand
summary: Mode-dependent actor reaction: when the UI overlay mode byte (work+0x48 -> +0x281) is not 7 it fires event command 0x18 through the event state; otherwise it plays the actor's default animation and returns 1.
evidence: The branch is clear (Event_OnTriggerCommand vs Field_Object_PlayDefaultAnim), but neither the named caller Field_SceneObject_SpawnByTypeB nor any string explains why this is a 'break command', so the old wording is retained only as a maybe_.

name: Ui_GuideWindow_CommitPendingPage
summary: Commits the guide window's pending page: binds the stored pane (f_58) into the message-window slot at f_4C+0x1E18, marks the message window dirty (f_94 = 1) and invokes its layout virtual at f_11C+0x78.
evidence: CORRECTED: the named callers Ui_GuideWindow_NextPage and Ui_GuideWindow_LayoutPage only need the 'make the stored page current' step, and the body performs exactly that bind + dirty + layout sequence - no pane is pushed onto a stack, which the old 'PushPagePane' wording implied.

name: maybe_Field_Object_SelectIdleAnim
signature: void maybe_Field_Object_SelectIdleAnim(FieldObject* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Switches a field object to its default pose: notifies the children, resolves the party member record from self+0x273, selects keyed animation 1 (or 8 when the member record flag 0x10 is set), records the choice at +0x272, clears both animation slots and enters sub-state 4.
evidence: The keyed select (Container_KeyedList_Select with keys 1/8) and the named party accessor func_0035EB98 are clear, but 'idle' is an interpretation of the keys and the owning class is not fixed by any named caller.

name: maybe_Ui_ListWindow_IsRowActivated
summary: Row predicate: asks the row object at rowIndex through its virtual +0x20 whether it is active and, when the current row differs and is valid, asks the current row's +0x24 slot to compare itself with the candidate before answering 1.
evidence: The two-virtual protocol on the row-pointer array at +0x3C is clear and its callers are the named Container_KeyedList_Select / CommitSelection, but neither the 'activated' meaning nor the ListWindow class is confirmed by a named method.

name: maybe_Actor_SelectAnimEntry0
summary: Shared animation reset: runs the common prologue 0x005E7818 and, when the object has a keyed animation list at +0x60, selects and immediately plays key 0.
evidence: The named callee Container_KeyedList_Select(self+0x60, 0, 1) fixes the mechanism, and 198 callers across field, battle and UI code show it is a generic reset helper rather than an Actor-only method - which also weakens the 'Actor_' class label.

name: maybe_Model_SpriteAnimCallback
summary: Animation-slot callback: writes the sampled index/scale and a pair of interpolated values into the slot, calls the owner's virtual +0x4, and when the owner counter +0x40 is above 3 creates or replaces a 0x28-byte name-handle child in its container.
evidence: Seven of the eight source values arrive as damaged registers (unaff_r4..r7) because the Thumb calling convention was not recovered, so neither the argument order nor the owner class can be established; only the slot writes and the container child replacement are real.

name: Field_SceneObject_InitFromEntry
summary: Initialises a spawned field object from its 8-byte spawn entry: sets the visible/active byte f_45 from entry[7] and entry[5] != 0xFF, resolves the model variant via 0x0066B6D0(bagWork, entry[5], entry[6]) clamped to entry[0], and stores entry[5]/entry[6]/entry[2] in f_46/f_47/f_48.
evidence: Both named callers (Field_Scene_InitObjectTable, Field_Scene_UpdateObjectsFromTable) feed it spawn-table records, and the body reads exactly the documented 8-byte record layout; this is the field-object counterpart of the object factory.

name: Ui3D_ConstructListElement
summary: Constructor of the 0x50-byte UI3D draw-list element: obtains the object from the shared scene allocator, installs type table 0x0077B140 and clears the two id words at +0x48/+0x4C. The object table inserts it into the keyed tree by its record key.
evidence: The named callers Field_Scene_InitObjectTable / Field_Scene_UpdateObjectsFromTable allocate exactly 0x50 bytes, call this, set the type byte at +0x44 and insert the object into the keyed tree; table 0x0077B140 is the same type table as the named Ui3D_SlotMaskPanel_DeletingDtor, which confirms the UI3D prefix.

name: Field_ObjectSprite_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the 0x48-byte field object-sprite record: obtains it from the shared scene allocator, installs vtable 0x0077E314 and clears the two state bytes +0x45/+0x46.
evidence: The named callers allocate 0x48 bytes, call this constructor, then run func_0059AF20 on the result and insert it into the scene object tree; the vtable 0x0077E314 (not the stale header's 0x0059B048) is the object family's table.

name: maybe_Field_Object_Ctor_vt7673DC
summary: Constructor of another scene object type created by the field object factory: obtains storage through the shared scene allocator, installs vtable 0x007673DC and initialises the id/sentinel fields (+0x45 = 0xFF, +0x46 = 0xFFFF, +0x4A = 0xFF, +0x4C = 0x0FFFFFFF).
evidence: CORRECTED: the body is a constructor (allocation + vtable install + sentinel fields), not an 'InitShared' of the sprite class - the vtable 0x007673DC differs from the sprite ctor 0x0077E314. Its only caller is the named Field_Scene_UpdateObjectsFromTable object factory; the concrete class is unknown, so the vtable address is used as the honest discriminator.

name: maybe_Field_Object_Ctor_vt77635C
summary: Constructor of a tiny scene object holding one float: obtains storage through the shared scene allocator, installs vtable 0x0077635C and writes the -1000.0f 'no value yet' sentinel at +0x48.
evidence: CORRECTED: the function allocates and installs a vtable, so it is a constructor of one of the object types built by Field_Scene_UpdateObjectsFromTable, not necessarily a 'Ui_ValueHolder'. The -1000.0f sentinel (0xC47A0000) is the one concrete fact, and the class is still unknown.

name: maybe_Field_Object_Ctor_vt779F44
summary: Constructor of a small time/scale scene object: obtains storage through the shared scene allocator, installs vtable 0x00779F44, sets the 0.3f field at +0x48, clears +0x4C and sets the id byte +0x4D to 0xFF.
evidence: CORRECTED: it is a constructor, not a 'Field_ObjectHook' identified by any named method; its only caller is the named field object factory Field_Scene_UpdateObjectsFromTable, and the vtable 0x00779F44 is the only class discriminator available.

name: maybe_Field_Object_Ctor_vt77C298
summary: Constructor of a small scene object: obtains storage through the shared scene allocator, installs vtable 0x0077C298, sets the id byte +0x45 to 0xFF (the empty id) and clears the two state bytes +0x46/+0x47.
evidence: CORRECTED: the body is the standard 'allocate + install vtable + id sentinel' constructor used by the object factory Field_Scene_UpdateObjectsFromTable; the first pass's 'floor-map jump trigger' had no support in the body, and 'Ui_Object' is replaced by the neutral Field_Object with the vtable as discriminator.

name: maybe_Ui_SkillPanel_IsDetailOpen
summary: Global UI query: returns non-zero when the flag byte at GameWork+0x2767D is set. The skill panel's input and state handlers test it before opening the detail view.
evidence: Only the two named skill-panel handlers (Ui_SkillPanel_HandleInputB, Ui_SkillPanel_ApplyState) call it, but the body takes a value from an unrecovered register (in_r3) and no other function or string documents the +0x2767D flag, so its exact meaning stays unproven.

name: Ui_Window_SelectRowFromRef
signature: void Ui_Window_SelectRowFromRef(void* self, const UiItemRef* ref)
summary: Makes the display row named by a {index, kind} list-item reference the current row: resolves the reference with Ui_ListItemRef_ResolveRowSimple and copies the row into the data panel's current-row block through Ui_DataPanel_CopyRowIntoCurrent.
evidence: CORRECTED: the body does not use the window's own row array - it resolves a ref and copies the row into the savedata/data-panel current block at work+0x24A98, which is why the callee is Ui_DataPanel_CopyRowIntoCurrent; the old 'Ui_ListWindow' class label overstated what the call site proves.
